disclaimer: Visa requirements depend on the category and the issuing authority (ICP federally, GDRFA Dubai for Dubai-issued permits), and official federal summaries sometimes lag the issuing-authority pages. Fees shown as ranges are indicative all-in estimates unless a cost note cites an official fee schedule. Verify current eligibility, fees and durations with ICP or GDRFA before applying. Residence is digitally linked to Emirates ID.

visas.name: Tourist Visa (30 days)
best_for: scoping trips
short business visits
eligibility: Most nationalities require visa pre-arrival
Visa-on-arrival nationalities exempt
visas.process: Online via ICP/GDRFA portal, hotel sponsor, or airline. GDRFA Dubai targets 48-hour processing for 30 and 60 day tourist visas.
visas.cost_notes: GDRFA Dubai single-entry tourist visa issuance fee: AED 200 for 30 days plus 5% VAT (AED 210); AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation and AED 500 in-country fees apply if the visitor is already inside the UAE. The AED 700 upper bound is a legacy estimate of airline, hotel or agent packages (service charges, insurance) and is not an official fee.

visas.name: Tourist Visa (60 days)
best_for: longer scoping trips
extended family visits
visas.cost_notes: GDRFA Dubai single-entry tourist visa issuance fee: AED 300 for 60 days plus 5% VAT (AED 315); in-country fees as for the 30-day visa. The AED 1,200 upper bound is a legacy estimate of agent packages and is not an official fee.

visas.name: Visa on Arrival (14 or 60 days)
best_for: eligible nationalities and qualifying residence-permit holders arriving without a pre-arranged visa
eligibility: Nationals of the standard visa-on-arrival countries (per the current ICP list)

Since 25 June 2026: ordinary-passport holders of Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, the Philippines, Kenya and South Africa (plus accompanying family members), provided they hold a valid residence permit from the US, an EU member state, the UK, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada

Indian passport holders: the qualifying-document list widened in June 2026; residence or visas from Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and Canada now qualify in addition to the earlier US, EU and UK list
visas.verified_note: MOFA announcement of 25 June 2026 re-checked 2026-10-13: nationalities, qualifying residence-permit countries, AED 100 (14 days, extendable once) and AED 250 (60 days, non-extendable) unchanged.
visas.overstay_note: AED 50 per day is the standard overstay fine; no change, new amnesty or grace period dated 28 September to 20 October 2026 was found on ICP or GDRFA channels (the last disruption-related grace period ran 10 June to 9 July 2026).

visas.name: Investor / Partner Visa
best_for: anyone with a UAE trade license
eligibility: Active UAE trade license
Either mainland (DET) or free zone
Sponsor is the founder's own company
process_steps: Residence visa stamping (now digital, no sticker since 2022)
visas.cost_notes: AED 5,000 to 8,000 is an indicative all-in estimate (entry permit, status change, medical, Emirates ID, establishment card) not published as a single official fee; confirm with the licensing authority or free zone.

visas.name: Property Investor Visa (2 years, Dubai)
best_for: owners of completed Dubai residential property below the AED 2M Golden Visa threshold
eligibility: Sole owners: the AED 750,000 minimum property value was removed in April 2026, so a completed Dubai residential property of any value can qualify, subject to the usual conditions
Jointly owned property: each co-owner needs a registered share worth at least AED 400,000 (previously each co-owner had to meet the AED 750,000 threshold)
Mortgaged or instalment-purchased property: bank NOC plus proof that at least 50% of the value or AED 375,000 has been paid
Property must be completed, with the title deed registered with DLD
visas.change_note: The relaxed thresholds appeared on the DLD-affiliated Cube Centre platform around 29 April 2026 and were reported by Khaleej Times and Gulf News (Fragomen alert 8 May 2026). No formal decree or announcement was issued, so treat the exact thresholds as subject to confirmation. Note the channel discrepancy: the update surfaced on Cube Centre even though intake had formally moved to GDRFA on 11 April 2026, and it is unclear which platform is authoritative for eligibility rules.
visas.process_note: Since the GDRFA-DLD MoU of 11 April 2026, Property Residency applications run through a single GDRFA Dubai channel (document intake, DLD-fed property valuation and title verification, and visa issuance), superseding the earlier DLD Cube / Taskeen application path. Officials framed this as service integration, not a change to eligibility thresholds.
visas.official_page_note: The GDRFA Dubai service page 'Issuance of a residence permit for the owner of a property' (checked 2026-10-13) lists: property fully constructed (undeveloped plots excluded), ownership certificate from the competent registry, property fully owned by the applicant, property habitable, and monthly income of at least AED 10,000 or proof of financial solvency for the residence period. Fees: AED 200 permit, AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation, AED 500 in-country, AED 20 delivery (plus AED 100 per year beyond two years). Applications go through DLD-approved Amer centres. The page does not mention the joint-ownership or mortgaged-property relaxations reported via Cube Centre, so those remain subject to confirmation.

visas.name: Employment Visa
best_for: salaried role with a UAE employer
eligibility: Valid job offer from UAE-registered employer
Employer holds an active MOHRE quota or free zone equivalent
visas.work_permit_system_note: MoHRE relaunched the work-permit system on 7 June 2026 around 13 permit types (recruitment from outside the UAE, transfer, family-sponsored, temporary, mission, part-time, juvenile 15-18, student training, UAE/GCC national, Golden Residency holder, trainee UAE national, freelance, private tutoring; several with 2-year validity). Supporting-document requirements were eliminated and mandatory data fields cut roughly 75-97% for certain permits, with unified digital channels and roughly 2-working-day processing. The referenced e-consultation was scheduled to close on 30 July 2026; its expiry does not establish that any proposed rule took effect.
visas.ai_screening_note: From May 2026 all new work-permit applications are screened by a joint ICP-MoHRE AI and robotics platform that scores skills, education, experience and knowledge against ICP identity records and labour-market data, with automatic approval for strong matches and human adjudication for borderline files.

visas.name: Golden Visa (Specialized Talent)
best_for: scientists
doctors
engineers
specialists in priority fields
eligibility: Requirements depend on the talent category; scientists and other exceptional talents may need competent-authority nominations rather than a salary test.
For the skilled-professional route: UAE employment, MOHRE professional level 1 or 2, a recognised bachelor degree or equivalent, and any required professional licence.

The GDRFA Dubai skilled-professional page specifies at least AED 30,000 monthly salary and 6 months of bank salary transfers; confirm salary components and any additional case-specific evidence with the authority.
visas.cost_notes: Plus dependent visa fees. GDRFA lists AED 1,100 permit fee, AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation, AED 500 in-country and AED 20 delivery, with the issuance fee rising AED 100 per year beyond two years; medical, Emirates ID and insurance are extra, so the AED 2,800 to 9,500 range is an all-in estimate.
visas.process: Apply through ICP or GDRFA Dubai/Amer under the applicable subcategory. Residence is self-sponsored; the skilled-professional route still requires qualifying UAE employment.
visas.process_note: In Dubai, the GDRFA-DLD MoU of 11 April 2026 merged Golden, Retiree and Property residency services into a single GDRFA Dubai channel (service integration only; eligibility thresholds unchanged).
visas.eligibility_note: A blanket 24-month salary-history requirement across all specialized talents is not supported by the official pages (re-checked 2026-10-13). Salary alone does not establish eligibility; GDRFA states the permit is cancelled if salary falls below AED 30,000 or the contract ends.

visas.name: Golden Visa (Real Estate Investor)
best_for: property investors with AED 2M+ in UAE real estate
eligibility: Property worth AED 2 million or more (single or combined); for a share in jointly owned property, the share itself must be worth at least AED 2 million (GDRFA Dubai)

Mortgaged property is accepted: ICP requires the financing to come from an approved local bank, and GDRFA Dubai places a lien on the property and bars disposal during the permit term. Traditionally a substantial paid-in share was required for mortgaged or off-plan property; industry reports say this was dropped, but no official decision has been found (see unverified_note).
Off-plan units totalling at least AED 2 million qualify under ICP if bought from an approved developer authorised by the competent local authority
In Dubai the value is certified by a DLD property status statement (or a valuation from a DLD-licensed office)
visas.unverified_note: UNCONFIRMED: industry reports from around February 2026 claim the requirement to have paid 50% (or AED 1 million) of an off-plan or mortgaged property before applying was removed, with the full purchase price recorded on the Oqood counting toward the AED 2 million threshold regardless of the amount paid (developer or bank NOC still required). The ICP Golden Residency page (updated 10 September 2026) and the GDRFA Dubai investor page (checked 2026-10-13) accept mortgaged and off-plan property without stating any minimum paid percentage, but neither explicitly records the removal, and no DLD or ICP decision number has been found. Note the tension with the 2-year property visa rules, which still reference 50% or AED 375,000 paid for mortgaged property.
visas.process_note: Since the GDRFA-DLD MoU of 11 April 2026, Dubai Golden Residency applications linked to real estate run through a single GDRFA Dubai channel with DLD-fed property valuation and title verification (service integration only; eligibility thresholds unchanged).
visas.jurisdiction_note: The ICP Golden Residency page (updated 10 September 2026) and GDRFA Dubai both describe 10 years for real-estate investors; the u.ae Golden visa overview still describes 5 years for real-estate investments. Confirm duration and mortgage/off-plan conditions with the issuing authority.
visas.cost_notes: GDRFA lists AED 1,100 permit, AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation, AED 500 in-country and AED 20 delivery, plus AED 100 per year beyond two years; DLD certificates, medical, Emirates ID and insurance are extra, so the AED 3,800 to 9,500 range is an all-in estimate.

visas.name: Golden Visa (Entrepreneur)
visas.duration_label: 10 years (ICP and Dubai routes; u.ae overview still says 5 years)
best_for: founders of revenue-generating SMEs
founders with a prior venture exit
eligibility: ICP published route (page updated 10 September 2026): own or be a partner in a UAE-registered SME in an approved field with annual revenues of at least AED 1,000,000, with the venture idea approved by an accredited incubator, the Ministry of Economy or a relevant local authority; OR be a founder of one or more ventures previously sold for a total of at least AED 7,000,000. Comprehensive health insurance is required.

Dubai GDRFA route: Dubai Future Foundation nomination plus one of: a pioneering project registered with the Ministry of Economy or local authorities with AED 1 million annual income, an incubator or Ministry of Economy project with AED 2 million income, or a founded project sold for at least AED 7 million. Nomination does not guarantee approval.
The AED 500,000 project-valuation test cited in earlier versions of this pack no longer appears on the ICP or GDRFA pages and should not be relied on.
visas.jurisdiction_note: ICP and GDRFA Dubai now both describe 10 years, but with different evidence routes (ICP: revenue or exit value with incubator/ministry approval; Dubai: Dubai Future Foundation nomination). The u.ae Golden visa overview still lists 5 years and a generic project-value test. Confirm the applicable route before applying.
visas.cost_notes: GDRFA lists AED 1,100 permit, AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation, AED 500 in-country and AED 20 delivery, plus AED 100 per year beyond two years; the AED 2,800 to 5,000 range is an all-in estimate.

visas.name: Green Visa (Skilled Employee)
best_for: skilled employees with a valid MOHRE work permit
eligibility: Valid employment contract in the UAE with a MOHRE work permit
MOHRE skill level 1, 2, or 3
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
AED 15,000 minimum monthly salary
visas.process: Self-sponsored after obtaining a qualifying employment record.
visas.verified_note: ICP Green Residency page (updated 12 September 2026) re-checked 2026-10-13: thresholds unchanged.

visas.name: Green Visa (Freelancer / Self-Employed)
best_for: freelancers and self-employed professionals
eligibility: Freelance / self-employed permit from MOHRE
Bachelor's degree or specialized diploma
Annual freelance income of at least AED 360,000 in each of the past two years (about AED 30,000 per month), OR proof of financial solvency for the residency duration
visas.process: Self-sponsored. Requires MOHRE freelance permit first.
visas.verified_note: ICP Green Residency page (updated 12 September 2026) re-checked 2026-10-13: thresholds unchanged.

visas.name: Freelance Permit (TECOM / GoFreelance)
best_for: solo professionals in tech, media, education, design
eligibility: Recognised qualification or portfolio in a permitted activity
Application via TECOM, GoFreelance, or other free zone freelance program
visas.cost_notes: GoFreelance advertises its package at AED 7,500 per year (conditions apply), with the residence visa (AED 4,600 for one year, AED 5,042 for two) and AED 2,000 establishment card charged separately. The AED 20,000 upper bound covers other free zone programmes and is an estimate.

visas.name: Virtual Working Programme
best_for: remote employees of foreign companies who want UAE residency
eligibility: Employment contract with a foreign (non-UAE) employer
USD 3,500 minimum monthly salary (per the GDRFA Dubai service page and u.ae, re-checked 2026-10-13)
Health insurance valid in the UAE
visas.cost_notes: The cited GDRFA page is for the entry visa to complete residence formalities: AED 200 plus 5% VAT (AED 210). For inside-country applications it lists AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation and AED 500 in-country fees (AED 730 total on those components). Medical, Emirates ID, residence-permit and insurance costs are separate.
visas.unverified_note: UNCONFIRMED: some aggregators claim the income floor rose to USD 5,000 per month for employed applicants and that required health-insurance cover rose to AED 500,000. Neither figure appears on the official GDRFA service page or the u.ae page as of 13 October 2026, so treat them as unconfirmed.
visas.income_evidence_note: The cited GDRFA entry-visa service page requests proof of monthly income but does not specify a universal bank-statement period. Confirm the statement period and residence-permit documents for the actual application channel.

visas.name: Retirement Visa
best_for: age 55 and older with assets or income
eligibility: Age 55 or older at the time of retirement
Worked for not less than 15 years, inside or outside the UAE (mandatory, in addition to the financial test below)
Then ONE of the two financial routes must be met
Route A: own property in the UAE worth AED 1,000,000 or more AND hold financial savings of AED 1,000,000 or more (both are required, this is not an either/or)
Route B: annual income of at least AED 180,000 under the federal ICP rule, or AED 240,000 (AED 20,000 per month) for applications filed in Dubai
visas.eligibility_note: The property and savings amounts in Route A are cumulative. A frequent misreading treats them as alternatives, which understates the requirement by AED 1 million.
visas.process_note: Since the GDRFA-DLD MoU of 11 April 2026, Retiree Residency services in Dubai run through a single GDRFA Dubai channel together with Golden and Property residency (service integration only; eligibility unchanged).
visas.verified_note: Re-checked 2026-10-13. GDRFA Dubai: 55 years of age, at least 15 years of service, then either property worth AED 1,000,000 AND a deposit of AED 1,000,000 (a deposit held abroad must be moved to a UAE institution within 60 days of issuance unless invested in the UAE), or fixed annual income of at least AED 240,000 with six months of bank statements. u.ae: same structure with AED 180,000 federal income and AED 240,000 for Dubai.
visas.cost_notes: GDRFA lists AED 2,280 residence fees and AED 575 Emirates ID fee for the 5-year permit (including AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation, AED 500 in-country and AED 20 delivery components); medical and insurance are extra.

visas.name: Family / Dependent Visa
best_for: spouse and children of UAE residents
eligibility: Sponsor (the UAE resident) holds a valid residence visa
Sponsor minimum salary AED 4,000, or AED 3,000 plus employer-provided accommodation (per u.ae)
Attested marriage and birth certificates
visas.cost_notes: Per dependent. AED 5,000 to 7,500 is an indicative all-in estimate (permit, medical, Emirates ID, insurance, attestation); no single official fee is published.
visas.eligibility_note: The official federal page (re-checked 2026-10-13) states 'a minimum salary of AED 4,000 or AED 3,000 plus accommodation' without an additional universal basic-salary-only rule. Confirm acceptable evidence for the sponsor with ICP or GDRFA.

myth_busters.claim: A lifetime UAE Golden Visa can be bought for AED 100,000 by Indian and Bangladeshi nationals through overseas consultancies
myth_busters.note: ICP again formally denied this in late January 2026 after the claims resurfaced on social media (the original July 2025 Rayad Group story had already been debunked, and Rayad Group publicly apologised). ICP called the reports without legal basis, reiterated that all Golden Visa applications go exclusively through official government channels with no external advisory body approved, and warned of legal action under cybercrime law. The ICP Golden Residency page (updated 10 September 2026) lists only renewable 10-year categories, with no lifetime or nationality-specific nomination route.

upcoming.name: GCC unified tourist visa (Grand Tours)
upcoming.note: The unified GCC tourist visa pilot has slipped again and is now expected in Q4 2026, linking Dubai International with Bahrain International first (QR-code validation, ICP data sharing), with Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait joining in early 2027 if successful. Indicative pricing floated around USD 100 for single-country and USD 120-130 for a multi-country 60-90 day permit. The Q4 2026 Dubai-Bahrain pilot detail comes from secondary aggregators, so treat this as an expected timeline, not a live product.
upcoming.status_check: Re-checked 2026-10-20: still not live. No official launch date, application portal, fee or validity has been published by ICP or the GCC General Secretariat. The latest primary-adjacent statement remains the GCC Secretary General's 6 September 2026 remark (Khaleej Times, 8 September 2026) that the visa would 'see the light soon', with no date; nothing new was found for 28 September to 20 October 2026, so the Q4 2026 Dubai-Bahrain pilot remains an expectation, not a confirmed start.
upcoming.source_note: The VisaHQ pilot article cited earlier returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-20 and was replaced with a secondary Travel News report (4 February 2026) that attributes the end-2026 UAE-Bahrain pilot to the UAE Minister of Economy; its fee figures are a draft proposal.

last_refresh_scope: Targeted refresh of 2026-10-20: searched ICP, GDRFA Dubai, u.ae, WAM and the Dubai Media Office for visa and residency decisions dated 13 to 20 October 2026. Changed: the dead VisaHQ source for the GCC unified visa pilot (HTTP 404) was replaced with a secondary Travel News report, and the GCC and overstay re-check dates were advanced. Checked with no change: the ICP Golden Residency page (still dated 10 September 2026: entrepreneur AED 1,000,000 revenue or AED 7,000,000 prior exit; real estate AED 2,000,000 with approved-bank loans and approved-developer off-plan units, no paid-in percentage stated), the ICP Green Residency page (still dated 12 September 2026: AED 15,000 salary, AED 360,000 freelance income), GDRFA Dubai news (latest item 14 September 2026) and ICP media centre (no rule change). No new ICP or GDRFA residency, fee, overstay-fine or amnesty decision, no new visa category and no GCC unified visa launch was found; the GDRFA and Awqaf Dubai waqf-donor Golden route dates from October 2025 and is outside this pack's founder categories. Still unverified: the off-plan and mortgaged 50% paid-in removal for the Golden real-estate route, the Cube Centre joint and mortgaged thresholds for the 2-year property visa, the upper bounds of the tourist, investor, family and freelance cost ranges, and the GCC Q4 2026 pilot timing. Not a full re-verification of every field in this pack; full_review_date is preserved.
